event: Israeli drone strikes resulted in two deaths in Rafah and Gaza City.

verified_facts.statement: Israeli drone strikes occurred in Rafah and Gaza City resulting in two deaths
verified_facts.note: Core event claim; specific locations and casualty count stated in event

verified_facts.statement: Hamas carried out an attack on October 7, 2023
verified_facts.note: Widely documented historical fact; referenced in multiple framings as context

verified_facts.statement: Gaza has a high population density
verified_facts.note: Demographic fact accepted across framings; relevant to civilian casualty context

verified_facts.statement: The International Court of Justice has received a case alleging genocide under the Genocide Convention
verified_facts.note: South Africa v. Israel case filed January 2024; factual procedural status

verified_facts.statement: The United States has provided military aid to Israel
verified_facts.note: Long-standing documented policy; referenced in US political fallout framing

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Over 200 Palestinian journalists have been killed in Israeli strikes during this conflict
unverified_shared_claims.note: Press Freedom framing cites this; Committee to Protect Journalists maintains a tally, but exact number and attribution to Israeli strikes specifically requires verification against CPJ database

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Nearly 2 million Palestinians have been displaced from their homes
unverified_shared_claims.note: Genocide/Ethnic Cleansing framing emphasizes this; UN agencies report displacement figures, but precise number and timeframe require current source verification

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Hamas embeds military infrastructure in civilian areas including UN and civilian facilities
unverified_shared_claims.note: IDF Operational Precision framing asserts this; some documentation exists (UN reports on weapons caches), but extent and systematic nature are contested

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Israel has deployed AI-assisted or autonomous targeting systems in Gaza drone strikes
unverified_shared_claims.note: Autonomous Drone Technology framing claims this; no official Israeli confirmation; based on eyewitness testimony and inference from drone deployment patterns

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Israel has banned independent foreign press access to Gaza
unverified_shared_claims.note: Press Freedom framing states this; press organizations have documented restrictions, but characterization as total ban vs. severe limitation is debated

points_of_disagreement: Whether the two deaths (and broader drone strike pattern) constitute war crimes / IHL violations vs. lawful military operations under self-defense doctrine
Whether civilian deaths result primarily from Israeli targeting decisions vs. Hamas's deliberate use of human shields and civilian infrastructure
Whether the cumulative scale of strikes and displacement constitutes genocide/ethnic cleansing vs. proportionate counter-terrorism response
Whether Israeli drone strikes systematically target journalists to suppress documentation vs. incidental casualties in legitimate military operations
Whether Israel's drone technology deployment represents a test case for autonomous lethal weapons governance vs. standard precision military practice
Whether the US should leverage military aid to constrain Israeli operations vs. maintain support for Israeli security needs
The moral and legal weight of Israeli security concerns (Oct. 7 aftermath, ongoing Hamas threat) vs. Palestinian civilian protection obligations
shared_foundation.summary: All framings accept that Israeli drone strikes killed two people in Rafah and Gaza City, that Gaza is densely populated, that the US provides military aid to Israel, and that the ICJ is hearing a genocide case. The disagreements are entirely interpretive: whether these strikes are lawful self-defense or war crimes; whether civilian deaths reflect Israeli targeting choices or Hamas's use of shields; and what legal, moral, and political consequences should follow.

framings.name: International Law & War Crimes Accountability
framings.question: Did this drone strike violate IHL — specifically the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution — and who should be held accountable?
framings.key_claim: Israeli drone strikes in densely populated Gaza constitute a pattern of IHL violations that may amount to war crimes and demand ICC investigation.
framings.description: This framing applies international humanitarian law to the strike, asking whether the IDF distinguished between combatants and civilians, took feasible precautions, and whether civilian harm was proportionate to any military gain. It centers accountability mechanisms — ICC, UN bodies, domestic investigations — as the appropriate response.
framings.emphasizes: Civilian death tolls, IHL principles (distinction/proportionality), absence of Israeli investigations, ICC jurisdiction, UN resolutions, historical pattern of drone-strike casualties
framings.downplays: The military intelligence basis for the strike, Hamas's role in embedding fighters among civilians, the Oct. 7 context, Israeli security obligations
sample_headlines: Israeli Air Strikes That Killed 44 Civilians Further Evidence of War Crimes – New Investigation (Amnesty International, May 2024)
Gaza Exposes the Limits and Dangers of IHL's Proportionality Rule (JURIST, Dec. 2025)
Precisely Wrong: Gaza Civilians Killed by Israeli Drone-Launched Missiles (HRW, June 2009/updated)

carriers.name: Amnesty International
carriers.excerpt: The ICC should investigate as war crimes three Israeli air strikes that killed 44 Palestinian civilians, including 32 children
carriers.role_evidence: Amnesty's detailed field investigations originated the legal war-crimes framing applied to specific Rafah/Gaza drone and air strikes

carriers.name: Human Rights Watch
carriers.excerpt: Israeli forces failed to take all feasible precautions to verify that these targets were combatants, as required by the laws of war
carriers.role_evidence: HRW coined the IHL-accountability framing for Israeli drone strikes on civilians as early as 2009, establishing the analytical template reused throughout the 2023-2026 war

carriers.name: UN OHCHR
carriers.excerpt: The pattern of Israeli strikes…indicates that the IDF may have systematically violated the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precautions
carriers.role_evidence: OHCHR's formal thematic report gave official UN institutional weight to the IHL-violation framing

carriers.name: Lawfare Media
carriers.excerpt: Israel's tolerance for civilian casualties is now completely out of step with that employed by the U.S. and its coalition partners
carriers.role_evidence: Lawfare's legal analysis reached national-security and legal practitioner audiences early, amplifying the proportionality-focused accountability frame

carriers.name: Georgetown Journal of International Affairs
carriers.excerpt: Israel's distortions of IHL proportionality to legalize unlimited child casualties violate the general rule imposing special protection of children
carriers.role_evidence: Academic journal article arguing the proportionality distortion threatens IHL's global framework, amplifying the frame into scholarly and policy circles

carriers.name: UN Human Rights Council Commission of Inquiry
carriers.excerpt: Israel's operations in Gaza have constituted war crimes, crimes against humanity, and violations of IHL and IHRL
carriers.role_evidence: UN HRC commission formally found war crimes by both Israel and Hamas, giving the accountability framing authoritative multilateral institutional backing

framings.name: Legitimate Military Self-Defense
framings.question: Were these strikes a lawful exercise of Israel's right to self-defense against a terrorist organization that initiated the conflict?
framings.key_claim: Israeli drone strikes in Rafah and Gaza City are necessary and legally justified counter-terrorism operations against Hamas, which is responsible for the Oct. 7 massacre and continues to use civilians as shields.
framings.description: This framing places the strikes within the broader context of Israel's post-Oct. 7 campaign, arguing the IDF is exercising a sovereign right of self-defense under UN Charter Article 51. It foregrounds Hamas's culpability for civilian suffering by embedding fighters in civilian areas.
framings.emphasizes: Oct. 7 Hamas attack, Israeli military's stated targeting of armed operatives, Hamas's use of civilian infrastructure, IDF claims of precision and prior warnings, Israeli soldier casualties
framings.downplays: Palestinian civilian death toll and suffering, questions of proportionality, displacement and humanitarian crisis, independent verification failures
sample_headlines: IDF Strikes Senior Hamas Operative in Gaza City Responsible for 2002 Beersheba Bombing (The Media Line, 2024)
Israel's Struggle with the Information Dimension during the Gaza War (Army University Press, 2024)
IDF: Troops Eliminated Militant Cell, Destroyed Launcher Used to Attack Israeli Soldiers (various IDF statements)

carriers.name: IDF Spokesperson / Israeli Government
carriers.excerpt: Israel's military said it had spotted suspects who were operating a drone that posed a threat to its troops
carriers.role_evidence: The IDF's official statements after each strike consistently originate the self-defense/targeted-militant framing used by pro-Israel media

carriers.name: BESA Center for Strategic Studies
carriers.excerpt: To protect themselves, the terrorist launching teams operate from within the safe haven declared by Israel, near the road on which the humanitarian supply convoys travel
carriers.role_evidence: Israeli think-tank providing detailed analytical amplification of the human-shields/self-defense framing to English-language policy audiences

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: IDF kills moneyman who it says transferred millions to military wing
carriers.role_evidence: Leading English-language Israeli outlet that mass-amplifies the IDF's framing of individual strikes as targeted counter-terrorism operations

carriers.name: Army University Press (U.S. Army)
carriers.excerpt: Israel has implemented various strategies and platforms to counter adversary information operations during its ongoing fight against Hamas
carriers.role_evidence: U.S. military academic publication that contextualizes Israeli operations within a counter-terrorism information-war frame, lending institutional U.S. credibility

framings.name: Human Cost & Civilian Suffering
framings.question: Who are the specific people killed and injured, and what does their suffering tell us about the human reality of these strikes?
framings.key_claim: Each Israeli drone strike represents identifiable Palestinian lives — families, children, journalists — destroyed in a densely populated enclave with no safe refuge.
framings.description: This framing centers the named and unnamed victims: their identities, last moments, family members left behind, and the overcrowded conditions (Rafah as a 'last refuge') that make every strike catastrophic. It foregrounds the human and emotional texture of loss rather than legal or military abstractions.
framings.emphasizes: Named victims, family grief, children killed, medical testimony, displacement context, survivor and eyewitness accounts, total cumulative death toll
framings.downplays: Military objectives, Hamas's role, legal frameworks, political dimensions, Israeli casualties and suffering
sample_headlines: 'People Were Literally Burned Alive in Their Tents' — Doctor Describes Rafah Airstrike Scene (NPR, May 2024)
Eyewitnesses in Gaza Say Israel Is Using Sniper Drones to Shoot Palestinians (NPR, Nov. 2024)
Israeli Strikes on Rafah Kill 22, Including 18 Children (NPR/AP, April 2024)

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: 'People [were] literally burned alive in their tents,' Smith told NPR
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's on-the-ground correspondents and eyewitness/medical accounts consistently drive the human-cost framing to a broad US public audience

carriers.name: WAFA (Palestine News Agency)
carriers.excerpt: PRCS paramedics saying they evacuated the bodies of four victims after an Israeli army drone targeted a group of people
carriers.role_evidence: Palestinian official wire service that first reports individual strike deaths, naming victims and locations, originating the human-cost factual record

carriers.name: Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: The second strike killed 17 children and two women, all from the same extended family, according to hospital records
carriers.role_evidence: AP's sourcing from named hospitals and specific family accounts makes it a leading mass-amplifier of individual-victim human-cost framing

carriers.name: Airwars
carriers.excerpt: Documented allegations of civilians killed and injured…spotlighting often under-reported cases of harm
carriers.role_evidence: Conflict-monitoring NGO that systematically documents and archives individual civilian-harm incidents, giving the human-cost framing evidentiary depth

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: At least 10 Palestinian people were killed while lining up to buy flour in an Israeli attack on Rafah
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's Gaza-embedded correspondents provide consistent high-volume amplification of civilian-victim stories to a global English-language audience

framings.name: Press Freedom & Journalistic Targeting
framings.question: Are Israeli drone strikes systematically eliminating Palestinian journalists, and what does this mean for accountability and the flow of information from Gaza?
framings.key_claim: Israeli drone strikes have killed over 200 Palestinian journalists covering Gaza, constituting what press-freedom groups call a systematic effort to suppress independent documentation of the war.
framings.description: This framing focuses specifically on the targeting — deliberate or negligent — of journalists by Israeli drones, and the resulting information blackout. It connects individual strikes to the broader closure of Gaza to international press, framing journalism deaths as an attack on democratic accountability.
framings.emphasizes: Named journalist victims, Committee to Protect Journalists tallies, Israel's ban on independent foreign press access, the chilling effect on documentation, AFP/AP/Al Jazeera organizational responses
framings.downplays: IDF's stated military justifications for specific strikes, Hamas's own restrictions on reporting, non-journalism civilian casualties
sample_headlines: Israeli Drone Strike on Vehicle Kills 3 Journalists in Gaza (CPJ, Jan. 2026)
Israeli Drone Strike Kills Al Jazeera Correspondent Mohammed Wishah in Gaza City (Democracy Now!, April 2026)
More Than 200 Palestinian Journalists and Media Workers Have Been Killed in Gaza Since the War Began (CPJ/AP, 2026)

carriers.name: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
carriers.excerpt: CPJ rejects characterization of the strike that killed Reuters journalist Issam Abdallah as a 'mistake'
carriers.role_evidence: CPJ is the primary institutional originator of the press-freedom framing, documenting and naming every journalist killed by Israeli fire in Gaza

carriers.name: Democracy Now!
carriers.excerpt: Gaza's Media Office says Wishah's killing reflects a 'systematic targeting and assassination' of Palestinian journalists by Israel
carriers.role_evidence: Democracy Now! amplifies the systematic-targeting narrative to a left-progressive US audience with high repetition

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / NPR
carriers.excerpt: Among the dead were three Palestinian journalists who were killed while filming near a displacement camp
carriers.role_evidence: PBS/NPR brought the journalist-targeting framing to mainstream US broadcast audiences with named victims and AFP organizational response

carriers.name: Agence France-Presse (AFP)
carriers.excerpt: 'Abdul was much loved by the AFP team covering Gaza. They remember him as a kind-hearted colleague'
carriers.role_evidence: AFP's institutional statement demanding investigation for its killed contributor gave the press-freedom framing wire-service authority and global reach

carriers.name: Al Jazeera
carriers.excerpt: Al Jazeera says it will pursue legal action against those responsible
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's announcement of legal action formalized the press-freedom framing into a litigation-backed institutional posture

framings.name: IDF Operational Precision & Human-Shield Complexity
framings.question: Did the IDF follow its stated rules of engagement, and were civilian deaths unavoidable given Hamas's deliberate use of densely populated civilian areas?
framings.key_claim: Civilian deaths in Israeli drone strikes, while tragic, result from Hamas's deliberate embedding of military infrastructure in civilian areas, forcing the IDF into impossible targeting decisions.
framings.description: This framing accepts that civilians were killed but attributes primary moral and legal responsibility to Hamas's tactical choice to operate from schools, mosques, hospitals, and residential buildings. It foregrounds IDF claims of precision targeting, advance warnings, and intelligence-based operations while contesting the framing of strikes as indiscriminate.
framings.emphasizes: Hamas's use of civilian human shields, weapons caches in UN/civilian facilities, IDF advance warning procedures, claimed precision and intelligence verification, IDF soldier casualties
framings.downplays: IHL scholars' arguments that human-shield presence does not negate proportionality obligations, independent inability to verify IDF targeting claims, scale of civilian casualties
sample_headlines: Weapons Found in UNRWA Compound: Rockets, Remote-Controlled Bombs, Drone Being Assembled (BESA Center, 2024)
IDF: Strike Targeted Militants Using Convoy as Cover; No NGO Personnel Hurt (BESA Center, 2024)
IDF Uses Tanks and Intelligence Information; Claimed Militants Eliminated at Site Used for Attacks Against IDF (Times of Israel, 2024)

carriers.name: IDF Spokesperson (official statements)
carriers.excerpt: IDF claims it took measures to reduce civilian harm, including precision-guided munitions, aerial surveillance, and advanced intelligence assessments
carriers.role_evidence: IDF's post-strike statements systematically originate the precision-targeting/human-shield complexity framing

carriers.name: BESA Center for Strategic Studies
carriers.excerpt: Hamas operates from within the safe haven declared by Israel, near the road on which humanitarian supply convoys travel, or inside schools, mosques, and UNRWA facilities
carriers.role_evidence: Bar-Ilan University think-tank that provides detailed English-language analytical amplification of the human-shield complexity framing to Western policy audiences

carriers.name: Drone Wars UK (critic role)
carriers.excerpt: While advocates present drones in humanitarian terms as effectively minimising civilian casualties…serious concerns have been raised by human rights organisations
carriers.role_evidence: UK-based drone-monitoring group explicitly challenges the 'precision' framing, documenting the gap between IDF precision claims and documented civilian harm

carriers.name: Duke University / Judicature (legal scholarship)
carriers.excerpt: IHL violations by one party do not relieve the opposing party's obligation to comply, and cannot be used to justify similar violations in response
carriers.role_evidence: Duke legal scholars explicitly rebut the human-shield framing as an excuse, clarifying that IHL obligations are non-reciprocal

framings.name: Genocide / Ethnic Cleansing
framings.question: Do the pattern and scale of Israeli strikes — including in Rafah, the 'last refuge' — constitute genocide or ethnic cleansing of Palestinians under international law?
framings.key_claim: Systematic Israeli drone and air strikes across all of Gaza, including the final refuge of Rafah, combined with displacement of nearly 2 million people, constitute genocide or ethnic cleansing that the ICJ has begun to address.
framings.description: This is the most expansive framing, moving beyond individual-strike accountability to claim that the cumulative pattern of violence, displacement, and destruction meets the legal or political threshold for genocide. It explicitly references the ICJ's Genocide Convention proceedings and invokes the 1948 Nakba as historical context.
framings.emphasizes: Scale of cumulative destruction, ICJ Genocide Convention proceedings, mass displacement ('largest since 1948 Nakba'), near-total population displacement, destruction of civilian infrastructure, famine conditions
framings.downplays: Hamas's military activities, Oct. 7 causation, the legal specificity required for a genocide finding, distinctions between individual strikes and a broader policy
sample_headlines: Israel Has Proceeded with Its Genocidal Offensive in Complete Disregard of the ICJ (WAFA, Oct. 2024)
UN Commission: Israel's Ensuing Offensive Killed More Than 67,000 Palestinians, Displaced 90% of Gaza's Population (Snopes citing UN, Feb. 2026)
Israeli Aggression Has Resulted in Forceful Displacement — Palestine's Largest Mass Exodus Since the 1948 Nakba (WAFA, 2024)

carriers.name: WAFA (Palestine News Agency)
carriers.excerpt: Israel has proceeded with its genocidal offensive on the war-torn Strip in complete disregard of the International Court of Justice
carriers.role_evidence: Palestinian Authority's official wire service consistently originates the genocide/Nakba framing in its coverage of every individual strike

carriers.name: Democracy Now!
carriers.excerpt: His death brings the total number of journalists killed in Gaza since October 2023 to 262
carriers.role_evidence: Democracy Now! regularly frames cumulative killing statistics within a genocide narrative, amplifying it to a US progressive audience

carriers.name: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
carriers.excerpt: The ICJ ordered Israel in a legally binding decision to halt its military offensive in Rafah, which may violate its obligations under the Genocide Convention
carriers.role_evidence: The ICJ's provisional measures ruling formally institutionalized the genocide-convention framing, giving it unprecedented legal weight

carriers.name: UN Commission of Inquiry (via Snopes/reporting)
carriers.excerpt: Israel's ensuing offensive killed more than 67,000 Palestinians and displaced an estimated 90% of Gaza's population in what a United Nations commission declared a…
carriers.role_evidence: UN commission's characterization of the scale of displacement as historically unprecedented gives genocide-adjacent framing authoritative multilateral grounding

carriers.name: Pro-Palestinian protest movement / social media
carriers.excerpt: Protesters march to denounce the Biden administration's support of Israel, which has killed thousands of Palestinian civilians
carriers.role_evidence: US street protest movement and social-media accounts drove mass adoption of the genocide framing in American political discourse, pressuring the Democratic Party

framings.name: US Political Fallout & Foreign Policy Leverage
framings.question: How do Israeli drone strikes in Gaza affect US domestic politics, American credibility, and the Biden/Trump administrations' ability to broker peace?
framings.key_claim: Each Israeli strike that kills Palestinian civilians deepens US political divisions, strains the administration's credibility with Arab American voters and allies, and complicates hostage-deal diplomacy.
framings.description: This framing treats the strikes primarily as inputs into American political calculations — how they affect the ceasefire negotiations, US arms-supply debates, electoral politics (Michigan, Arab American vote), and the bipartisan competition between Biden and Trump for credit on the Gaza file.
framings.emphasizes: US arms transfers, White House pressure on Netanyahu, bipartisan hostage-deal politics, electoral consequences, Trump vs. Biden credit-claiming, US diplomatic leverage
framings.downplays: Palestinian human suffering as a primary concern, IHL compliance questions, the interests of Gazans themselves
sample_headlines: Biden Risks Deepening Middle East Conflict as Pressure Mounts to Respond (CNN, Jan. 2024)
Gaza Ceasefire-Hostage Deal Is a Rare Bipartisan Victory in US Politics (The Forward, Jan. 2025)
Israel Launches Renewed Strikes in Gaza Less Than 3 Weeks Into Trump's Ceasefire Deal (NPR, Oct. 2025)

carriers.name: CNN Politics
carriers.excerpt: Biden risks deepening Middle East conflict with pressure to respond to deadly troop attack
carriers.role_evidence: CNN's White House-focused coverage consistently frames Gaza strikes primarily through the lens of US political and diplomatic consequences

carriers.name: The Forward
carriers.excerpt: Republicans and Democrats are uniting in support of the newly announced ceasefire-hostage deal, with both sides claiming their approach helped advance the agreement
carriers.role_evidence: The Forward's coverage of bipartisan credit-claiming for the ceasefire crystallizes the US-political-fallout framing for the American Jewish readership

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: The Israeli military began carrying out renewed strikes in the Gaza Strip, less than three weeks after President Trump brokered a ceasefire
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's ceasefire-violation coverage frames each resumed Israeli strike primarily as a diplomatic crisis for the Trump administration

carriers.name: Brookings Institution
carriers.excerpt: As Israel struggles to settle on a plan to successfully end the war in Gaza, the last thing it needs is a wider regional conflict — the same is true for President Biden
carriers.role_evidence: Brookings' analysis consistently frames Israeli military action through coinciding US-Israeli political interests and diplomatic constraints

carriers.name: Snopes / PolitiFact
carriers.excerpt: An online rumor alleged that Trump used Biden's 'exact deal' to end the war in Gaza — that's not true
carriers.role_evidence: Fact-checkers push back on the most partisan versions of the US-political-credit framing, distinguishing actual policy differences from partisan narrative

framings.name: Autonomous Drone Technology & Oversight
framings.question: What do these strikes reveal about the legal and ethical governance of drone warfare, AI-assisted targeting, and the global proliferation of armed unmanned systems?
framings.key_claim: Israel's widespread deployment of armed drones — including potentially AI-assisted targeting systems — in Gaza is a test case for the legality and global governance of autonomous lethal weapons technology.
framings.description: This framing zooms out from the individual strike to the technology enabling it: the role of AI-assisted targeting ('Lavender,' 'Gospel' systems), sniper drones, the history of Israeli drone development, and what Gaza's use of these systems means for international norms on autonomous weapons. It is primarily driven by investigative journalists, arms-control researchers, and drone-monitoring NGOs.
framings.emphasizes: AI/algorithmic targeting systems, sniper-drone eyewitness testimony, Israeli arms export model using Gaza as a 'test zone,' opacity of drone strike authorization, international norms vacuum
framings.downplays: Geopolitical cause of the conflict, Hamas's actions, legal frameworks already addressing drone use, humanitarian law principles that do apply
sample_headlines: Eyewitnesses in Gaza Say Israel Is Using Sniper Drones to Shoot Palestinians (NPR, Nov. 2024)
Israel's Drone Use Is Shrouded in Secrecy — DWUK Research Pieces Together the Evidence (Drone Wars UK)
Precise Strikes: Fractured Bodies, Fractured Lives — Israeli Drone Use 2014–2019 (Drone Wars UK)

carriers.name: NPR Investigations
carriers.excerpt: Sniper drone technology — distinct from that of other armed drones, which often carry bombs — does exist, and videos indicate the Israeli military has acquired it
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's investigative report on sniper drones — with named eyewitnesses and medical testimony — drove this technology-governance framing to a mainstream US audience

carriers.name: Drone Wars UK
carriers.excerpt: Israel's use of drones to launch attacks continues to be shrouded in secrecy and denial despite clear evidence
carriers.role_evidence: Drone Wars UK originated the 'Gaza as test zone for drone warfare' framing and has maintained the most comprehensive English-language audit of Israeli drone use since 2009

carriers.name: Human Rights Watch
carriers.excerpt: Each and every Israeli missile strike during Operation Cast Lead would be registered on video — drone operators record everything viewed
carriers.role_evidence: HRW's 'Precisely Wrong' report pioneered the transparency-and-oversight angle on Israeli drone targeting, calling for video records to be used in accountability proceedings

carriers.name: Airwars
carriers.excerpt: Matching Israeli military strike footage to civilian casualties on the ground to reveal full human cost of 'precise' campaign
carriers.role_evidence: Airwars systematically cross-references IDF strike footage against civilian-harm records, amplifying the technology-accountability framing with empirical data

gap_analysis: Missing: Palestinian armed group operational tactics and civilian proximity decisions; Israeli domestic security concerns and threat assessment specifics; regional geopolitical actors (Iran, Hezbollah, Egypt) and their strategic interests; technical/forensic analysis of strike accuracy and intelligence sourcing; humanitarian aid disruption and economic consequences; victim family/community perspectives and local accountability mechanisms separate from international frameworks.
